units.source: Distinguish "have ever done" from "did (a specific time)"
units.translation: Distinguir "haber hecho alguna vez" de "hice (un momento específico)"

units.context: Scenario: Making Plans & Talking About Time · Lesson: Past Experiences · grammar (Verb + 过 (experience) vs. Verb + 了 (specific completed event))
units.source: "过" asks/states general life experience ("have you ever..."); 了 marks a specific completed instance, often paired with a time word like 去年.
units.translation: "过" pregunta o expresa una experiencia general de vida ("¿alguna vez has..."); 了 marca un hecho concreto y terminado, a menudo junto a una palabra de tiempo como 去年.

units.context: Scenario: Making Plans & Talking About Time · Lesson: Past Experiences · grammar (Verb + 过 (experience) vs. Verb + 了 (specific completed event))
units.source: Using 过 when giving a specific time (should use 了): "我去年去过北京" is less natural than "我去年去了北京" when a specific time is given.
units.translation: Usar 过 al dar un momento específico (debería usarse 了): "我去年去过北京" suena menos natural que "我去年去了北京" cuando se da un momento concreto.

units.translation: "还没...过" combina "todavía no" (还没) con el marcador de experiencia (过): "todavía no he hecho X".

units.source: Using 不 instead of 没 to negate 过 - 过 is always negated with 没, never 不.
units.translation: Usar 不 en vez de 没 para negar 过: 过 siempre se niega con 没, nunca con 不.

units.source: "在哪儿吃的？" and its answer "在...的" use 的 to focus on the location detail of something already established as past.

units.source: Adding 了 instead of 的 when the focus is specifically on WHERE, not just THAT it happened - 的 is used to emphasize the detail being asked about.
units.translation: Agregar 了 en vez de 的 cuando el enfoque está específicamente en DÓNDE, no solo en QUE ocurrió: 的 se usa para resaltar el detalle que se está preguntando.

units.context: Scenario: Making Plans & Talking About Time · Lesson: Future Plans · grammar (打算 (planning to) / 要 (going to, more decided) / 会 (will, prediction/promise))
units.source: "打算" states an intention still somewhat open; "要" is a firmer decision; "会" is used for predictions or promises about the future.
units.translation: "打算" expresa una intención todavía algo abierta; "要" es una decisión más firme; "会" se usa para predicciones o promesas sobre el futuro.

units.context: Scenario: Making Plans & Talking About Time · Lesson: Future Plans · grammar (打算 (planning to) / 要 (going to, more decided) / 会 (will, prediction/promise))
units.source: Treating all three as fully interchangeable - each carries a different shade of certainty/intention that changes the nuance.
units.translation: Tratar las tres como totalmente intercambiables: cada una lleva un matiz distinto de certeza o intención que cambia el sentido.
